reason: While some regular people are treated respectfully (Manoah and his wife receive an angel's message with piety), the broader portrayal of regular people in this Samson narrative is predominantly negative. The Israelites 'continue to do evil in the sight of the Lord' (v. 1); Samson's wife from Timnah weeps and manipulates him into betraying the riddle; the men of Judah betray Samson to the Philistines; Delilah repeatedly deceives and seduces him for payment; and the general populace mocks him. Rather than favorable, most ordinary people in this text are depicted as weak, treacherous, complicit in wrongdoing, or antagonistic. The narrative structure elevates only the exceptional hero (Samson) and his parents as worthy of respect, while other regular people are shown as failures or enemies.
